sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a house in La Vergne, TN?
sections.html:
Selling in La Vergne usually means choosing between an agent, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash buyer who skips the repair list. Your pick should follow the condition of the house and your deadline.

The Census QuickFacts table shows a city that grew to 42,146 residents by July 2025, from 32,588 in 2010. Owners live in 74.0% of homes, those homes have a 2020-2024 median value of $309,900, and households average 3.03 people.

  • Agent listing: suits a house with few problems and an owner willing to wait through showings and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: the commission stays with you, along with the advertising and the contract work.
  • Cash buyer: a fit for houses with postponed repairs, a tenant in place or an estate to wrap up.

sections.h2: Where is La Vergne and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
La Vergne is in northern Rutherford County, southeast of Nashville, and it borders Nashville's Antioch area to the northwest, Smyrna to the southeast and Percy Priest Lake to the northeast, according to Wikipedia. Interstate 24 and U.S. routes 41 and 70S run through town, and workers here spend 31.6 minutes getting to their jobs on average.

The settlement dates to 1852, the town was first incorporated in 1860 and then reincorporated in 1972, the year after Firestone (later Bridgestone) opened a plant. Growth since has come from warehousing and distribution: an Amazon distribution center and the ICEE Corporation headquarters arrived in 2020, and a BJ's Wholesale Club in 2023. Lake Forest Estates, with more than 3,100 homes, is described as the largest single subdivision in Tennessee, so many La Vergne sellers compete against similar houses on nearby streets.

sections.h2: Which schools serve La Vergne homes?
sections.html:
Rutherford County Schools runs the public schools inside La Vergne. The list on Wikipedia, which cites the county district, includes LaVergne High School, LaVergne Middle School, LaVergne Lake Elementary, Rock Springs Elementary, Roy Waldron School and Simon Springs Community School.

School zones follow the county district's boundaries and can differ from street to street, so ask Rutherford County Schools which school an address is zoned for before you tell a buyer. Residents under 18 are 28.6% of the city and residents 65 or older are 7.9%, per the Census Bureau, which describes a young, family-heavy population.

sections.h2: How do La Vergne city and Rutherford County property taxes work?
sections.html:
La Vergne bills its own city property tax, and Rutherford County bills a separate county tax, so a seller should confirm both are current. The city's Tax Department page shows a rate of $0.5363 on each $100 of assessed value, set by the Board of Mayor and Aldermen.

The city cannot take county tax payments. County bills go to the Rutherford County Trustee at the Judicial Building, Suite 302, Public Square North in Murfreesboro, phone 615-898-7705. Taxes owed for more than two years are handled by the Rutherford County Chancery Court at 615-898-7860, and any old balance should be cleared before closing.

sections.h2: What permits and neighborhood rules affect a La Vergne seller?
sections.html:
The city's Title 13 municipal code sets upkeep rules that code officers enforce, and a buyer's inspector will notice violations. The Permits, General Rules and Ordinances page lists several that come up on resale houses.

  • Grass and weeds may not grow past one foot within 100 feet of a property line, residence or right-of-way.
  • A disabled or inoperable vehicle may not sit on the property for more than two weeks.
  • Swimming pools need a fence or barricade, and a pool permit costs $50 with a plot plan.
  • Unfit structures must be repaired or removed, or the city can step in.
  • Quiet hours run from 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.

Deck permits are $50 and shed permits depend on square footage. Electrical permits are state permits, and Rutherford County Building Codes at 615-898-7734 handles them. For anything else, the Codes Department number is 615-213-2624.

sections.h2: What does La Vergne offer buyers outside the house itself?
sections.html:
Water is the main draw. Percy Priest Lake sits on the northeast edge of the city, and the city lists boat launches at Hurricane Creek and camping at Poole Knobs Recreation Area. Veterans Memorial Park, a 55-acre city park, has ball fields, tennis courts, a skate park, pavilions and trails.

The La Vergne Public Library holds more than 60,000 items, and the fall festival that grew from the Old Timers Festival, first held in 1972, takes place at Veterans Memorial Park. For 2020-2024 the Census Bureau reports $81,313 in median household income and a 15.1% poverty rate. If your house is within a short drive of the lake or the park, say so in any listing or offer conversation, since those are features a buyer can verify.

sections.h2: Can I sell a La Vergne house that is used as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
The sale is allowed, but the buyer should know how the city treats that use. The city's zoning ordinance, updated July 7, 2026, defines a short-term vacation rental as a dwelling unit used entirely for transient occupancy for which the city has issued the owner a business license under the municipal code.

The ordinance's use tables allow short-term vacation rentals in some districts outright and in others only with additional requirements, and its definition of residential use excludes rentals shorter than one month. Before you advertise a house as an income property, ask the La Vergne Tax Department at 615-793-3388 whether a business license is on file and what happens to it on a sale. The same office issues new business licenses.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a La Vergne sale?
sections.html:
A La Vergne deed is filed with the Rutherford County Register of Deeds, not at city hall. The state's deed transfer tax comes to 37 cents for every $100 of the price, per the state revenue department.

The Register's office states that it is not licensed to run title searches and never guarantees that a deed is free and clear, so use a title company for that work. Its recording policy keeps overpayments of $10 or less per document, and a document with too little money attached is returned the same day. The office also hosts a land-fraud alert service, MyLandAlert, an alert notification service meant to flag land fraud early.

faqs.q: Does a La Vergne seller owe the city tax at closing?
faqs.a: Any unpaid city balance should be settled at or before closing, and the buyer and seller work out the proration between them. The La Vergne Tax Department can give a payoff figure, and county taxes are a separate bill with the Rutherford County Trustee.

faqs.q: Where do I pay La Vergne property taxes?
faqs.a: City taxes go to the La Vergne Tax Department at 1500 E. Nir Shreibman Blvd., online through its tax search portal, or by phone at 877-580-5923. County taxes are paid to the Rutherford County Trustee in Murfreesboro.

faqs.q: Is there tax help for older La Vergne homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. The city tax office has taken applications for the state's tax relief program for elderly or disabled owners and disabled veterans, and the tax freeze for seniors goes through the Rutherford County Trustee by appointment and must be renewed every year. Ask the Trustee for this year's income limit.

faqs.q: Who inspects electrical work in La Vergne?
faqs.a: State of Tennessee deputy inspectors do. La Vergne takes part in the state electrical program, so electrical permits are state permits, issued by Rutherford County Building Codes or through the state's online system.

faqs.q: What decides the closing date on a La Vergne sale?
faqs.a: Title work and your mortgage payoff set the pace, and a buyer paying cash does not wait on a lender. Get the closing date in writing and confirm with the title company that city and county taxes are paid.
